sentences.text:
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2.

The petitioner filed the above claim petition under Section 166(1)(a) of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 20.04.2014.

According to the petitioner, on 20.04.2014, at 12 noon while he was riding a motor cycle from Kalpetta to Kozhikode a Tavera car bearing Registration No.KL 11 U 6309 driven by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner, hit against his motor cycle and as a result he fell down and sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the driver, the 2 nd respondent is the owner and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P.
is Rs.20,00,000/-.
The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of documentary evidence as Exts.A1 to A14 series and Ext.C1.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.12,01,600/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

9. Heard Smt. Celine Joseph, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri.
P.G. Ganappan, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.

sentences.text: The Point: In this case, the accident as well as valid insurance policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.

One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the appellant is that the notional income of the MACA NO.2755 OF 2017 2025:KER:55336 petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal is too low when compared to his salary.
The petitioner was working as Teacher in an aided School named SABMP UP School drawing a monthly salary of Rs.23,103/-.
Ext.A9 is the salary certificate produced by him to prove his salary.
At the time of the accident, he was aged 32 years.
The Tribunal has fixed his notional income at Rs.5,000/- on the ground that, because of the injuries sustained in the accident, there is no reduction in his salary.

11. As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2014 will come to Rs.9,500/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Considering the fact that in the accident the petitioner sustained very serious injuries including six fractures, that he had undergone four surgeries, that he was treated as impatient for a total period of 43 days and he had to avail leave for a period of 606 days, because of the injuries sustained in the accident, I hold that his notional income can be fixed at Rs.12,000/-.
12.

In the accident he sustained the following injuries:
(1) CT Scan of brain shows right frontal and left temporal multiple small hemorrhagic contusion, multiple MACA NO.2755 OF 2017 2025:KER:55336 hemorrhagic contusions in right basifrontal, high frontal and left temporal lobes.
(2) CT Scan abdomen & pelvis: perivesical haematoma with airpocket anterior to collapsed urinary bladder.
(3) Posterior dislocation of right hip-6 weeks post OP fracture right acetabulum.
(4) Healing left subtrochateric fracture with implant in situ.
13. As per Ext.C1 disability certificate issued by the Medical Board, his permanent disability as per the Mc Bride scale was assessed as 45% and as per the NIOH scale, it was assessed as 75%.
The Tribunal fixed his permanent disability as 45%.
He was treated as impatient for a total period of 43 days in three sessions.
In the meantime, he had undergone 4 surgeries also.
On 10.04.2025 the petitioner appeared in person and this Court noticed that even at that time he could walk only with difficulty.
The Tribunal, has accepted the permanent disability of the petitioner as per the Mc Bride scale as 45% and hence, I do not find any grounds to interfere with the same.
Therefore, the permanent physical disability of the petitioner is accepted as 45%, as fixed by the Tribunal.
14. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 32 years.

Therefore, 50% of the monthly income is to be added towards future MACA NO.2755 OF 2017 2025:KER:55336 prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v. Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 16, as held in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

sentences.text: Towards loss of earning, the Tribunal has awarded only Rs.25,000/-.
From Exhibit A9 salary certificate, it is revealed that the petitioner, a teacher by profession was getting a monthly salary of Rs.23,103/- per month.
It is also revealed that because of the injuries sustained in the accident he had to take leave for a period of 606 days, approximately 20 months.

Therefore, towards loss of income, the petitioner is entitled to get salary for a period of 20 months, which will come to Rs.4,62,060/- (23,103x20).
16.
Towards pain and suffering the Tribunal has awarded Rs.20,000/-.
Towards loss of amenities nothing was awarded.

Considering the fact that the petitioner sustained six fractures and he had undergone four surgeries and he was treated as impatient for 43 days and he had availed leave for 606 days because of the accident, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the head pain and suffering is too low and hence it is enhanced to Rs.1,50,000/-.
For the very same reasons he is entitled to get reasonable compensation on the head loss of amenities also.

Considering MACA NO.2755 OF 2017 2025:KER:55336 the facts, I fix the compensation on the head loss of amenities at Rs.1,50,000/-.
17.
Towards extra nourishment the Tribunal has awarded Rs.5,850/-.
Towards transportation only Rs.5,000/- was awarded.

According to the learned counsel for the appellant, the petitioner was to be treated as impatient for 43 days in four sessions and hence the compensation awarded on the above heads are on the lower side.
It is also submitted that the petitioner who is residing at Wayanad was to be treated at Kozhikode and as such considering amount was to be spent towards transportation.
Therefore, the compensation on the head transportation expense is enhanced to Rs.15,000/-.

Similarly, the compensation on the head extra nourishment is also enhanced to Rs.15,000/-.
18.
The petitioner has produced additional medical bills worth Rs.3,75,038/- towards the amount spent after the passing of the award.
Since the above claim is supported by medical bills, the petitioner is entitled to get a sum of Rs.3,75,038/- towards additional medical expense.

19. The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the petitioner had spent a sum of Rs.80,000/- towards the expense for physiotherapy and that Ext.A11 receipt produced in that respect was rejected by the Tribunal.
The Tribunal rejected the above receipt on the ground that MACA NO.2755 OF 2017 2025:KER:55336 Ext.A11 was not proved by examining the Physiotherapist.
Considering the seriousness of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and percentage of disability suffered by him, it is quite natural that he requires physiotherapy to recover from the injuries.
It is true that the petitioner has not examined the Physiotherapist to prove Ext.A11.
Therefore, considering the facts I hold that a sum of Rs.40,000/- can be awarded on the head expense for physiotherapy.
20. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

21. Therefore, the petitioner/appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.34,76,048/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:
